To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) one can apply a high capacity CNN to region proposals in order for it to learn to localize and segment the objects and (b) one can use a CNN pre trained on an auxiliary task to initialize a CNN for a target domain and fine tune the weights of the CNN for the target domain.

(1) CNNs can be used for bottom up object detection and segmentation, (2) one can learn a rich hierarchy of visual features by training a CNN on an auxiliary task, and (3) combining these features with region proposals yields state-of-the-art object detection performance.

(1) high capacity convolutional networks trained with a multi stage approach can learn a rich hierarchy of features that are useful for detecting objects in natural images and (2) the combination of high capacity CNNs and selective search region proposals yields state of the art object detection results on PASCAL VOC.
